title: RANT: You don't need a coach
summary: NH argues that almost no lifter, beginner or advanced, needs a paid coach: coaches mostly pre-digest freely available knowledge, many are incompetent or frauds, and coaching keeps clients helpless so they keep paying. He refuses to sell coaching, believes training knowledge should be free, and wants viewers to learn to program for themselves.

claims.claim: Most lifters, beginner or advanced, don't need a coach; it takes a very special individual to need coaching (e.g. competing as an advanced lifter or very specific needs).
Most of what a coach does is take freely available knowledge and pre-digest it for you.
Self-coached progress may be slower with setbacks or injuries, but those also happen with coaches, many of whom are not capable.
If you hire a coach, check credentials and history: any record of lying or bad behavior.
NH dislikes monetizing knowledge transfer: lifters should learn together as a community, and charging for knowledge you got for free is unjust.
NH will help in videos and comments but will never offer coaching, which he considers a scam about 99% of the time.
Coaches have an incentive to keep clients in perpetual helplessness so they keep paying.
Learn to make your own programs and to recognise a bad program; you don't need to be an elite athlete or coach, just willing to learn.
For form reassurance, use YouTube tutorials and listen to your body: if a lift doesn't feel right, the form probably isn't good.
